Hand-cut layered paper art, handcrafted stop-motion paper diorama aesthetic.

Create a title illustration for a children's story app, rendered entirely as handcrafted paper art.

STYLE:
Strongly emphasize the physical nature of real paper: visible paper fibers, subtle cardstock grain, crisp cut edges, slightly imperfect hand-cut contours, and tiny natural variations in shape. Use simple, graphic silhouettes and charming handcrafted forms rather than realistic modeling. Each object should be simplified into a small number of flat paper shapes, generally using only one or two solid tones per element. Avoid excessive internal detail.

Create depth primarily through PAPER LAYERING, not through realistic light-and-shadow modeling. Individual paper pieces should sit slightly above or behind neighboring layers, creating narrow, soft, clearly separated cast shadows along their cut edges, like stacked cardstock mounted with tiny spacers. Keep all shapes internally flat and evenly colored. No volumetric shading inside leaves, bean pods, soil, stones, or plants.

CRITICAL STYLE RULE:
Flat paper shapes must remain visibly FLAT.
Do not create volume by shading the interior of a shape.
A leaf, bean pod, cloud, stone, or plant must look like a flat silhouette cut from cardstock, not a miniature three-dimensional object.
Depth may appear ONLY through overlapping separate sheets and the thin cast shadow underneath their cut edges.

Use occasional very shallow debossed or embossed paper details for simple veins, folds, grooves, or decorative lines, but keep these extremely subtle. They should look pressed into paper rather than sculpted.

COMPOSITION (most important):
A landscape 16:9 home-screen banner picture that fills the WHOLE canvas edge to edge: a full-bleed rectangular paper diorama scene (no cream sheet, no window, no border, no frame, no ornaments around it). Only 3 or 4 flat paper depth planes. It shows an inviting moment from the story that does NOT reveal how the story ends (no ending, no resolution, no reward, no final happy reunion): Christmas Eve in a cosy living room beside a decorated Christmas tree: the kind old godfather (bald head with grey side hair, plum-purple long coat, exactly like the reference) bends forward and holds out the wooden nutcracker doll (tall navy-blue top hat, red soldier jacket with gold buttons, navy trousers, black boots) to the girl Clara (brown bob hair, cream blouse, peach apron, mauve skirt), who reaches for it with delight; her brother Fritz (curly brown hair, orange vest, navy trousers) peeks curiously from behind a red armchair. Snowy night outside the window. Keep the main characters large and inside the CENTRAL area of the picture, well away from every edge (the picture will be cropped a little on all sides). Keep the LOWER-LEFT third and the LOWER-RIGHT corner calm and simple (plain ground, floor or snow, no faces, no important objects) because a title and a button will be placed there. Keep the background very simple with one or two elements, no tiny details; faces clearly visible.

FACE (characters only): a simple cut-paper face — two round dot eyes, a tiny dot nose, a small curved paper-strip mouth, two round pale-pink paper cheeks. No realistic eyes, no eyelashes, no glossy highlights.

Match the characters (same hair colour, clothes, faces, head size) and the paper-art style of the reference images exactly (same faces, clothes, proportions). 

LIGHTING:
Use soft, diffuse studio-style lighting from the upper-right (soft moonlight with a warm lamp and candle glow), mainly to reveal the edges and spacing of stacked paper layers.
Shadows should be short, soft, restrained, and consistent.
They must feel like paper-layer shadows, NOT realistic sunlight shadows cast by natural three-dimensional objects.

OVERALL FEELING:
Warm, tactile, whimsical, handcrafted, elegant, slightly imperfect, sophisticated paper craft, photographed straight from the front.

NO text.
NO photorealism.
NO glossy surfaces.
NO realistic 3D modeling.
NO inflated or rounded forms.
NO clay-like volume.
NO gradients.
NO painterly rendering.
NO airbrushed shading.
NO realistic sunlight shadows.
NO deep ambient occlusion.
NO thick beveled edges.
NO plastic appearance.
NO felt or fabric appearance.
NO fur-fibre texture.
NO title, NO letters anywhere.

Use case: children's picture-book app home-screen card thumbnail (ages 3-4), layered paper-cut collage art.
Reference images: pictures and character sprites from the tale "호두까기 인형". Keep the SAME characters with the SAME designs, colours, outfits, faces and paper-art style, and the same setting and palette. Characters are layered coloured-paper cut pieces with faces; props have no faces.

The top part is a calm warm living-room wall with one window showing a snowy night.

- The TOP 38% of the picture is calm, simple background only (sky, wall, night sky, etc. that belongs to the scene): no faces, no heads, no characters, no busy objects, no text there. A moon, a few soft clouds or a distant hill line at the far edges are fine.
